name: MathlibAnnex.Analysis.CStarAlgebra.Representation.surjective_of_irreducible_of_finiteDimensional
title: Full operator image in finite dimension

content.display_title: Full operator image in finite dimension
content.one_sentence_role: Constructs a preimage of an arbitrary operator by separately lifting its self-adjoint real and imaginary parts.
content.natural_language_statement: Let $A$ be a unital complex $C^*$-algebra and $H$ a nonzero finite-dimensional complex Hilbert space. If $\pi:A\to\mathcal B(H)$ is an irreducible unital representation, then $$\forall T\in\mathcal B(H)\ \exists c\in A:\ \pi(c)=T.$$
content.assumptions: No singleton condition, faithfulness or separability of $A$ is assumed. The finite-dimensionality and nontriviality hypotheses concern $H$.
content.conclusion: The image of $\pi$ is all bounded operators on $H$.
content.proof_summary: Interpolate each self-adjoint operator on the whole finite-dimensional space, then use the real-imaginary decomposition.
proof_steps: For a self-adjoint bounded operator $S$, apply [Self-adjoint interpolation on a finite-dimensional subspace](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/CStarAlgebra/ExactInterpolation.lean#L403-L419) to the irreducible $\pi$, the finite-dimensional subspace $E=H$, and this $S$. The theorem supplies a self-adjoint $a\in A$ with $\pi(a)x=Sx$ for every $x\in E$ (and a norm bound which is not needed here). Since $E=H$, equality on all vectors gives $\pi(a)=S$. This is packaged in [Preimages of self-adjoint operators on the whole finite-dimensional space](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/CStarAlgebra/Representation/FullImage.lean#L24-L36).

For an arbitrary $T$, define $$\operatorname{Re}T=(T+T^*)/2,\qquad\operatorname{Im}T=(T-T^*)/(2i).$$ Both operators are self-adjoint, so Step 1 gives $a,b\in A$ with $\pi(a)=\operatorname{Re}T$ and $\pi(b)=\operatorname{Im}T$.
Use the same two preimages to set $c=a+ib$. Complex linearity gives $$\pi(c)=\pi(a)+i\pi(b)=\operatorname{Re}T+i\operatorname{Im}T=T.$$ This constructs the required preimage of each $T$.
